<result># Review: `fix/eof-ends-session` (issue #6)

## Verdict

The fix is right and the design decisions you're second-guessing are, with one exception, the ones I'd have made. Centralising every player read into `readinput()` is the correct shape, the two `buf[strlen(buf)-1]` out-of-bounds reads were real latent bugs worth fixing on the way past, and the six-case `eof.sh` is a good test — I confirmed all six fail against `main` (status 13, output at the 256 KB ceiling, no farewell) and pass here, and that `main` floods 20 MB in under 5 s where the branch now emits 1180 bytes. I also confirmed plain mode and `-f` mode are byte-identical to `main` on a seeded tournament journey. Two things need attention before this ships: **Ctrl-D does not end the session in full-screen mode** (I reproduced it — ncurses in `cbreak()`+`echo()` treats `^D` as an ordinary character, so the player gets `UNRECOGNIZED COMMAND` and a command list instead of a sign-off), which means the branch's headline interactive behaviour only holds in one of the two modes and `eof.sh` case 6 gives false confidence because it silently runs the plain fallback. And **this fix quietly disarms `tests/journey.sh`**: I verified that removing the final answer from the journey script — the exact truncation the byte ceiling was invented to catch — now passes with `journey OK`. Needs changes.

## Answers to your questions

**Farewell + exit 0 mid-game — right call, but the sign-off is visually incomplete.** Keep the farewell. For an interactive Ctrl-D it is exactly right, and inventing a second ending for a game this small would be worse than reusing the one it has. But compare what the player actually sees:

```
COMMAND>                                     COMMAND>
May the Great Bird of the Galaxy roost...
                                             ******************************************************

                                             Do you want to play again?
                                             May the Great Bird of the Galaxy roost...
   (EOF)                                        (quit)
```

The `*****` band is this game's established "the session is over" punctuation — it's what `stars()` exists for — and its absence makes the EOF exit read as though the game fell over rather than signed off. Mirroring the quit path's `skip(2); stars(); skip(1);` before the farewell costs one line and makes both endings look like endings. That is my main answer to "does it read like they quit deliberately": right now it reads like *less* than quitting, not like quitting.

**A distinguishing marker: yes, but in the game's voice, not as an exit status.** The game already has a bracketed system-message register — `[ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING...]`, `[IMPORTANT ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING -- HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]`, `[CONTINUE?]`, `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]`. A single line in that register before the farewell fits perfectly, tells a scripting player what happened, and gives a harness something to grep:

```
[Transmission ends.]

******************************************************

May the Great Bird of the Galaxy roost upon your home planet.
```

Only emit it when a game is actually in progress (i.e. not at the very first prompt or at the play-again prompt, where "input ran out" and "the player is done" are the same thing).

**Exit status — keep 0.** Every CLI whose idiom this borrows exits 0 on end-of-input: `python`, `bc`, `sqlite3`, `ftp`, `mail`. A player doing `sst < moves.txt` inside a Makefile or a `set -e` script should not get a build failure because their game ended. And for a harness, exit status is the *wrong* channel anyway: the harness needs to distinguish "finished as scripted" from "ran out early", and both are legitimately non-failures of the program. The marker line above carries that information precisely; a non-zero status would conflate "input ended" with "the game crashed", which is worse for a harness, not better. Which brings me to:

**Should-fix 1 — `tests/journey.sh` no longer detects an under-supplied script.** I removed the trailing `n` from the journey's input (leaving the game one answer short at "Do you want to play again?") and ran the suite: `journey OK (3940 bytes)`. Before this branch, that same truncation was the runaway loop, caught by exit status and the byte ceiling. Now it exits 0, prints the farewell, and every `want` still matches. That matters because the desync class `journey.sh`'s own header warns about — a `[HIT SPACE BAR]` prompt eating a byte and shifting every subsequent command — now terminates in a way the test calls success. The remedy pairs naturally with the marker above: assert the marker is *absent*, or assert the game reached the normal ending (the `*****` band followed by `Do you want to play again?` immediately before the farewell). Either is one added check. Without it, this branch makes the suite weaker than it was, which is an odd outcome for a bug fix.

**Should-fix 2 — Ctrl-D does not end the session under `-t`.** `/home/scottdensmore/Developer/scottdensmore/super-star-trek/tui.c`, `tui_readline()`. Reproduced under tmux at 100x30: `tui_init()` sets `cbreak()`, which disables canonical mode and with it the tty's `VEOF` handling, so `wgetnstr()` never returns `ERR` for `^D` — it echoes a literal `^D` into the line and hands back a string. The player sees:

```
 COMMAND> ^D
 UNRECOGNIZED COMMAND. LEGAL COMMANDS ARE:
    SRSCAN    MOVE      PHASERS   CALL
    ...
```

I pressed it three times; the game never left. So the branch's stated interactive behaviour holds in plain mode only, and the two modes now disagree about what Ctrl-D means. Minimal fix inside `tui_readline()`: after `wgetnstr()`, treat a line consisting solely of `\004` as end of input and return `FALSE`. (The existing `ERR` branch is still worth keeping — it covers the terminal going away — it just isn't the path Ctrl-D takes.)

ui-review caught the most important thing in this change: **my fix silently disarmed the journey test.** A truncated journey now exits 0 and prints the farewell, so every existing assertion still matched — the exact input-desync class the byte ceiling was invented to catch had become a passing test. That marker does double duty. It also answers the reviewer's point that the EOF exit looked *less* than quitting: the ending now prints the game's `*****` band, so both endings look like endings, and a scripting player can tell which one they got.

And `eof.sh` reused one status file across cases, where a case dying early could inherit the previous case's success.

I also caught something on my own that the review flagged as whitespace noise: my `sed` had **stripped a carriage return** from `sst.h`, which is a CRLF file. Redone as a pure addition with endings intact.

On the reviewer's judgment questions, I kept exit 0 and the farewell — its argument that every comparable CLI (`python`, `bc`, `sqlite3`) exits 0 on end-of-input, and that a non-zero status would conflate "input ended" with "crashed", is right. The marker carries that information better than an exit code.

Verifier is running now, including a check on whether the `stars()` band is worth its 2.7s busy-wait — I kept it because the normal quit path pays exactly the same cost.

New review request, separate from #2/#3/#4/#16/#18 which you approved and which are all merged. Branch fix/eof-ends-session from main at 1b7eb70, fixing issue #6. All uncommitted: CMakeLists.txt, finish.c, osx.c, sst.c, sst.h, tests/journey.sh, tui.c, tui.h, plus new tests/eof.sh.

The bug (pre-existing): when player input runs out the game re-prompts forever. The verifier measured main sustaining ~60 MB/s of prompts; the branch replaces that with a 1.5 KB clean exit.

The fix:
1. sst.c — new `readinput()`, the single funnel for player input. On end of input: tui_shutdown(), linecount=0 (so it doesn't page on the way out), then "[Transmission ends.]", the stars() band, the usual farewell, exit(0).
2. scan() and finish.c's readline() both route through it. Both previously did `buf[strlen(buf)-1]` unconditionally, reading buf[-1] on an empty buffer; both guarded.
3. tui.c — tui_readline() returns int, and treats a line containing only Ctrl-D as end of input: cbreak() disables the tty's canonical EOF handling, so ^D arrives as an ordinary character and the player previously got "UNRECOGNIZED COMMAND" instead of an exit. Documented limitation: wgetnstr only returns on Enter, so under -t the Ctrl-D needs an Enter after it; plain mode ends on Ctrl-D alone. Fixing that properly means replacing wgetnstr with our own line editor.
4. osx.c — getch() ignored read()'s return and returned an uninitialised stack byte at end of input; now '\0'. The comment records why this path deliberately keeps playing while readinput() ends the session: it is the paging prompt, and quitting there would truncate end-of-game score output. The verifier confirmed that empirically by driving a self-destruct to death with input ending at the password — the full score still prints, then the next real prompt ends the session.
5. NEW tests/eof.sh (ctest `eof`, TIMEOUT 150, 15s per case): six cases stopping input at each point the game waits.
6. tests/journey.sh — asserts "Transmission ends" is ABSENT. This is the important one: ui-review found my fix had DISARMED the journey test, because a truncated journey now exits 0 with the farewell and every existing assertion still matched. Reproduced, and this closes it.
7. sst.h — declares readinput; a first attempt stripped a CR from this CRLF file, so it was redone as a pure addition (verifier confirmed 498/498 CRLF).

Two judgment calls I'd like your view on:
- The EOF ending prints the stars() band, which costs ~2.7s of busy-wait in prouts() and took the eof test from 3.4s to 19s. I kept it because the normal quit path pays exactly the same cost (verifier measured 2717ms vs 2716ms, both 54 asterisks), so the two endings are now indistinguishable in output and cost. The verifier agreed and noted the real fix, if it ever matters, is prouts()' clock() spin loop rather than a special-cased ending.
- exit(0) plus the farewell on a mid-game EOF, with "[Transmission ends.]" as the distinguishing marker rather than a non-zero status. ui-review argued every comparable CLI (python, bc, sqlite3) exits 0 on end-of-input and that a non-zero status would conflate "input ended" with "crashed".

Verifier PASSED: Debug 0 warnings, Release 17->14, `-Wall -Wextra` 33->30 with zero new warnings and exactly three fixed; 5/5 ctest in both types across three runs; 36 input-exhaustion points tested with no loops (including freeze/thaw filenames, self-destruct password, deathray, the Y/N loop, tournament score-recorded, and -f -t); plain and -f byte-identical to main under an LD_PRELOAD time shim; eof.sh POSIX/BSD-clean with traps on EXIT INT TERM HUP PIPE and zero leftovers across success, failure, flood, hang and SIGPIPE paths; the new journey assertion proven to have teeth and to appear 0 times in 10 legitimate journeys; line endings preserved file-for-file.

Please review as an expert in C and POSIX shell: correctness of readinput() and its call sites, the exit-from-deep-in-the-call-stack design (is exit(0) from inside scan() acceptable here, or should this unwind?), the Ctrl-D handling and its limitation, the getch() change, the test scripts, and whether the marker/band belong in the game's output at all. Read-only; end with an explicit approve or request-changes verdict.

1. `tests/eof.sh:69-71` — nothing asserts the `[Transmission ends.]` marker is *present*. I deleted `prout("[Transmission ends.]")` from a scratch copy of sst.c and **all five ctest tests passed**. **Nits**

2. `tests/eof.sh:105-108` — on failure you get only the FAIL lines, and the EXIT trap then deletes the work directory, so a CI failure leaves no evidence to read (journey.sh dumps 8 KB). Demonstrated with a missing binary: two FAIL lines and nothing else. Suggest retaining the failing case's capture and dumping a bounded tail before exit.

3. `sst.c:583` — `buf[0] = '\0'` immediately before `exit(0)` is a dead store; harmless, but it reads as though a caller might observe it.

**`exit(0)` from inside `scan()` — acceptable here; don't unwind.** I checked what gets skipped. There is no heap state to release, `exit()` flushes and closes stdout, and `atexit(tui_shutdown)` plus the explicit `tui_shutdown()` covers the terminal. Both file-writing paths read their filename via `scan()` *before* `fopen`, so no write is in flight. The single corner is `plaque()`, which opens the file before asking for the name — an input end there leaves an empty plaque file, closed cleanly by `exit()`, where main would have re-prompted forever. Unwinding instead would mean threading a sentinel through ~40 `scan()` call sites and auditing each for partial state: far more risk than this buys, and `emexit`'s `exit(1)` at sst.c:335 is existing precedent.

**`exit(0)` + marker over a non-zero status: right.** The precedent argument is sound, and a non-zero status would additionally break `set -e` harnesses whose input legitimately ends.

Byte-identical plain-mode output vs main — I did not rebuild your LD_PRELOAD time shim; the galaxy is clock-seeded, so I verified via the journey suite and code inspection of the untouched output paths instead.

### Verdict

**Request changes** — for finding 1 only. Everything else is sound: the design is right, the C is correct, two genuine latent bugs (`buf[-1]`, the uninitialised `getch` byte) are fixed along the way, and the tests are portable and clean. But the guard you correctly identified as "the important one" can itself still be disarmed silently, I demonstrated it end to end, and the fix is one `grep` in a file you are already touching. ## The bug

The game never learned that no answer was coming. It asked again, read nothing, asked again — roughly **60 MB of prompts per second**, for as long as anyone let it run. (During this work I accidentally left `main`'s binary going and produced 2.6 GB.) Anyone scripting the game or driving it from a harness got that instead of an ending, and it's why `tests/journey.sh` needs a byte ceiling at all.

Pre-existing; it predates the TUI work.

## The fix

Player input now goes through one function, and the stream ending finishes the session the way quitting does: the ship signs off, the usual band of stars, the usual farewell, exit 0.

**Exit 0 is deliberate.** Every comparable tool — `python`, `bc`, `sqlite3` — treats end of input as an ordinary ending rather than a failure, and a harness whose script legitimately runs out shouldn't see a crash. A non-zero status would also conflate "input ended" with "the game fell over".

**The two endings are alike but not identical.** `[Transmission ends.]` tells a scripting player which one they got — and the journey test now fails if it appears. Without that, a script stopping short looked exactly like a script that finished, which would have quietly made the suite *weaker* than before this fix. **Ctrl-D ends a full-screen game now.** Curses turns off the tty's own end-of-file handling, so `^D` used to arrive as an ordinary character and earn an `UNRECOGNIZED COMMAND`. Documented limitation: under `-t` it has to be followed by Enter, because `wgetnstr` only returns on Enter; plain mode ends on Ctrl-D alone.

## Two latent bugs fixed on the way past

Both readers indexed `buf[-1]` on an empty line, and `getch()` returned an uninitialised stack byte at end of input. Switched to a new branch 'fix/tui-panel-staleness'
## Problem

The TUI panels are meant to repaint from live game state before every prompt. Two cases break that contract:

1. **Paged output.** `tui_getch()` refreshes only the message window, so while the player is stepping through a `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` pause the quadrant and status panels can show state older than the text beside them.
2. **Play again.** After finishing a game and answering "yes", `d.date` is still non-zero from the previous game, so the panels display the *old* game's quadrant and status all through the new game's setup prompts.

Neither is a correctness bug in what the panels are allowed to reveal — the sensor-damage masking is unaffected — but both undercut "the panels always reflect now".

## Where

- `tui.c:95-98` — `tui_getch()` refreshes `wmsg` only; contrast `tui_readline()` at `tui.c:86`, which calls `tui_refresh_panels()` first.
- `tui.c:54` — `if (d.date > 0.0)` is the "is there a game yet" test, which stays true across a replay.

## Suggested approach

For (1), call `tui_refresh_panels()` in `tui_getch()` the way `tui_readline()` does.

For (2), give the panels an explicit "no game in progress" state rather than inferring it from `d.date` — e.g. clear it at the start of a new game, or track a separate flag set once setup completes. Prefer whichever keeps `tuifmt.c` free of curses and still unit-testable.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Panels are current when a paging prompt is on screen.
- [ ] Starting a second game shows empty (or clearly reset) panels during setup, not the previous game's data.
- [ ] `tests/test_tuifmt.c` still passes, extended if the "no game" state is expressible in the formatters.
- [ ] Plain mode unaffected.

New change to review as an expert in games and CLI games. Branch fix/tui-panel-staleness from main at 17d5d91, fixing issue #7. Small diff, all uncommitted: sst.c (+4), tui.c (+5/-2), tui.h (+3).

Issue #7 had two symptoms:
1. Paged output — tui_getch() refreshed only the message window, so while a [HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE] prompt was up the panels could be older than the text beside them.
2. Play again — after finishing a game and answering yes, the panels showed the PREVIOUS game's quadrant and status all through the new game's setup questions. I reproduced this exactly under tmux: second setup still showed "Quadrant 4 - 4" and "Stardate 3800.0" from the finished game.

Root cause of (2), confirmed by reading setup(): it resets `alldone` at its first line but `d.date` is not overwritten until much later, AFTER choose() has asked every setup question — so the old date is still live and the panels' `d.date > 0.0` test stays true.

The fix:
1. tui_getch() now calls tui_refresh_panels() the way tui_readline() does.
2. New `tui_ingame` flag replaces the `d.date > 0.0` inference. main() sets it FALSE before setup() and TRUE after, so panels are blank through the setup questions of every game including a replay. The frozen-game path (choose() returning early after thaw) still ends with it TRUE.

Verified under tmux at 100x30: during a second game's setup the panels are blank, and once it starts they show genuinely new data (stardate 4800 -> 4600, different grid). At 80x24 with a paging prompt up, the panels are drawn and current. Plain mode unaffected; 5/5 ctest; zero build warnings.

Please review the player-facing behaviour:
- Is blanking the panels during setup the right presentation, or would a player prefer something else there — a title, a hint, or the panels simply not drawn until the game starts? Right now they are empty bordered boxes with the titles "Quadrant" and "Status".
- Should the panels stay populated after a game ENDS (they do, until the next setup begins) or clear at that point? I chose to leave the final state visible while the score prints and the "play again?" question is asked, which seemed kinder, but I would like a second opinion.
- Does refreshing the panels at every paging prompt introduce any visual problem — flicker, a redraw the player notices mid-read, or a case where the panels changing under a [HIT SPACE BAR] prompt is confusing rather than helpful?
- tui_refresh_panels() calls newcnd() (recomputing the condition) when not docked, so that now runs at paging prompts too, not just before typed answers. Any gameplay-visible consequence I have missed?
- Anything else in the replay flow that still shows stale or wrong information.
Read-only: report findings with severity and a verdict, do not edit files.

The acceptance criterion allowed extending `test_tuifmt.c` "if the no-game state is expressible in the formatters" — it isn't; the decision lives in the curses layer. <result># Review: `fix/tui-panel-staleness` (issue #7)

## Verdict

Both fixes are correct and I reproduced both before/after states. The `tui_ingame` flag is the right call — inferring "a game exists" from `d.date > 0.0` was always a proxy for a fact the program actually knows, and replacing an inference with a fact is the better fix even setting the bug aside. I confirmed the replay flow now blanks the panels through the second game's setup questions and repopulates with genuinely new data (Stardate 2100 → 4400, new quadrant, new grid), and that panels are drawn and current at a `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` prompt at both 80x24 and 100x30. Plain mode is untouched and 5/5 ctest passes. Two things came out of driving this that you should act on: after the Enterprise is **destroyed**, the panels keep showing a healthy green ship at full shields next to "your starship is now an expanding cloud of subatomic particles" — which is the same lying-panel problem as issue #7, just at the other end of the game; and the `condit = IHRED` that `moving.c` sets deliberately before a tractor beam can now be silently reverted by the `newcnd()` inside a panel refresh at a paging prompt, which is the gameplay-visible consequence you asked about. Approve with should-fix items.

## Answers to your questions

**Blanking during setup: right, and the empty bordered boxes are the right presentation.** Keep them. The boxes are a promise — they tell the player where the scan and status *will* be, and the borders keep the message window anchored at the same row so the setup Q&A doesn't jump when the game starts. Filling them with a title card or a hint would be worse: the player is being asked four questions in a row and anything in the panels competes for attention with the question. Dropping the boxes entirely and letting the message window use the full screen would be actively bad, because the layout would then reflow the instant the game began. One small thing you already do right and should keep: the title reverts to plain ` Quadrant ` (no coordinates) when blank, so there's no orphaned "Quadrant 4 - 4" over an empty grid. Verified.

**Panels after a game ENDS: your instinct is right for survivable endings, wrong for death.** I self-destructed at 100x30 and got this, which is the finding I'd most want fixed:

```
x  1  . . . E . . . . . .   xx Stardate      2600.0
...                             Condition     GREEN
x  8  . . . . .   . . . .   xx Shields       DOWN, 100% 2500.0 units
                                Life Support  ACTIVE
      ...
 ************ Entropy of Enterprise maximized *********
 Your starship is now an expanding cloud of subatomic particles
 The Federation will be destroyed.
```

The `E` is still on the grid, Condition is GREEN, energy is 5000.00, shields are at 100%. At the single most dramatic beat in the game, the status panel is contradicting the narration. "Leave the final state visible while the score prints" is a kind idea and it works fine for `quit`, for running out of time, and for winning (Klingons Left 0 is a nice thing to leave on screen) — but when `alive == 0` the panel is describing a ship that no longer exists. There's a clean predicate for it: `finish.c` sets `alive = 0` in both death paths (lines 179 and 310). Setting `tui_ingame = FALSE` when the ship is lost — or, if you'd rather have one rule, blanking at the start of `finish()` for every ending and letting the epilogue own the screen the way plain mode does — resolves it. Severity: should-fix, because it is the same class of bug as issue #7 and it lands at the most memorable moment of a playthrough.

**Refreshing at paging prompts: no flicker, and no spoiler risk.** No flicker by construction — `tui_refresh_panels()` builds into the virtual windows and ends in one `doupdate()`, so ncurses emits only changed cells; holding space through several pages showed no flash in my captures. On the "changing under a prompt is confusing" worry, I checked the one case that would actually matter: `pause(1)`'s `[IMPORTANT ANNOUNCEMENT ARRIVING]`. I read all nine `pause(1)` call sites; for both the supernova (`events.c:91`) and the tractor beam (`events.c:137`) the pause fires *before* `snova()` and before the quadrant change, so the panels at the prompt show the pre-event state. The player is not shown where they're about to be yanked to before reading that they've been yanked. Good as-is.

**`newcnd()` at paging prompts: yes, there is one consequence you've missed.** `moving.c:38` sets `condit = IHRED` on purpose when a tractor beam will interrupt the move:

```c
	if (d.date+Time >= future[FTBEAM]) {
		trbeam = 1;
		condit = IHRED;
```

`newcnd()` recomputes condition purely from energy and quadrant contents, so it doesn't know about `trbeam` and will hand that RED straight back to GREEN. Any paging prompt between that assignment and the beam firing — and `pause(1)` for the announcement is exactly such a prompt, now that `tui_getch()` refreshes — reverts it. The player sees Condition GREEN at the very moment the game has decided they're in trouble. It's cosmetic (nothing downstream reads that RED; `newcnd()` is called again after the move anyway), and the window already existed via `tui_readline()`, but this branch widens it and it's the direct answer to your question. The deeper issue is that a *display* function is mutating global game state at arbitrary moments in a turn. I'd compute the condition into a local for display and leave `condit` alone, or drop the `newcnd()` call and accept that the panel shows what the game last computed. The comment "srscan does the same before showing Condition" is true but not equivalent: `srscan` runs when the player asks for it, between turns; the panel refresh runs mid-turn.

## Other findings

**Nit 1 — thawing a game shows blank panels while its report prints.** `choose()` calls `report(1)` after `thaw()` has fully loaded the game, but `setup()` hasn't returned yet so `tui_ingame` is still FALSE. If that report is long enough to page (likely at 80x24 with an attack report or casualties), the player gets a `[HIT SPACE BAR]` prompt with empty panels beside a report about a game that is completely loaded. I confirmed the flow works correctly at both sizes with a short report; the window is narrow but real. Setting the flag inside `setup()` on the frozen-game return (`if (choose()) { tui_ingame = TRUE; return; }`) would close it, at the cost of the flag being set in two places.

**Nit 2 — the flag is set in `main()`, which leaves `setup()` able to change state without the panels knowing.** Bracketing `setup()` from the caller is clear and I like that it reads as one obvious pair, but the truth it encodes ("the game state is now valid") belongs to `setup()`. If you take nit 1 you'll be setting it in two places anyway, at which point owning it inside `setup()` (FALSE at the top next to `alldone = gamewon = 0`, TRUE at both exits) is tidier and can't be forgotten by a future caller.

## Separate pre-existing bug found while driving this (not yours, but you're in the neighbourhood)

**`help <command>` displays nothing but blank lines in full-screen mode.** I ran `help move` in the TUI at both 80x24 and 100x30 and got `Spock- "Captain, I've found the following information:"` followed by page after page of empty lines and `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]`. I reproduced it identically on `main`, so it predates this branch — but it means the game's entire built-in manual is invisible to any `-t` player, which for a game of this complexity is severe.

The cause: `sst.doc` has CRLF line endings (`file` reports "ASCII text, with CRLF line terminators"), and `helpme()` strips only the `\n`, leaving a trailing `\r` on every line. In plain mode the terminal prints the text, then CR, then LF — fine. In ncurses, `waddstr` writes the text, the `\r` returns the cursor to column 0, and then `skip(1)`'s `\n` **clears the line from the cursor to end** before wrapping. I confirmed the mechanism with a minimal curses probe:

```c
waddstr(w, "LINE-A plain");    waddstr(w, "\n");
waddstr(w, "LINE-B with CR\r"); waddstr(w, "\n");
waddstr(w, "LINE-C plain");    waddstr(w, "\n");
```
renders as `LINE-A plain`, a blank line, `LINE-C plain`.

Worth its own issue. The fix is one line in `helpme()` (strip a trailing `\r` as well as `\n`), or more defensively in `tui_puts()`. It also means any future output line ending in `\r` will silently vanish in TUI mode, which is worth a note in AGENTS.md alongside the existing "all output through `prout`" rule.

## What I exercised

- Read the full diff plus `tui_refresh_panels()`, `main()`'s game loop, `setup()`/`choose()` (including the frozen-game early return), `newcnd()`, and all nine `pause(1)` call sites in `events.c`/`ai.c` to check for spoiler ordering.
- Built Debug, 5/5 ctest.
- tmux 100x30: full game → `quit` → panels correctly persist through the `*****` band and the play-again prompt → answered `y` → **panels blank through all four setup questions** → second game starts with genuinely new data (Quadrant 1-6/Stardate 2100 → Quadrant 5-8/Stardate 4400).
- tmux 80x24: startup paging prompt with blank panels (correct, pre-setup); in-game paging prompt with panels drawn and current.
- tmux 100x30: `destruct` + password → found the panels showing `E`, GREEN, 5000.00 energy, 100% shields alongside the destruction epilogue.
- Froze a game and thawed it in the TUI at both 100x30 and 80x24 to check the `choose()`-returns-early path (panels blank at the filename prompt, populated at the first `COMMAND>`).
- Built `main` in a scratchpad and reproduced the `help move` blanking there to establish it as pre-existing; wrote and ran a minimal ncurses probe to confirm the CR+LF line-clearing mechanism.
- Grepped every direct assignment to `condit` to find the `moving.c` interaction.
- No files modified — `git status` shows only your three.</result>

input.content:
## Problem

`help <command>` prints nothing but blank lines in full-screen mode. The game's entire built-in manual is invisible to any `-t` player.

Reproduce with the tmux recipe from AGENTS.md:

```sh
tmux new-session -d -x 100 -y 30 -s hp './build/sst -t; sleep 15'
# answer: regular / short / novice / <password>
tmux send-keys -t hp 'help move' Enter
tmux capture-pane -t hp -p
```

You get `Spock- "Captain, I've found the following information:"`, then page after page of empty lines with `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]`. The same command in plain mode prints 21 lines of documentation.

## Why it happens

`sst.doc` has CRLF line endings, and `helpme()` in `sst.c` strips only the `\n`, leaving a trailing `\r` on every line it prints.

In plain mode the terminal prints the text, then CR, then LF — harmless. Under ncurses, `waddstr` writes the text, the `\r` returns the cursor to column 0, and the following `\n` **clears the line from the cursor to end** before wrapping. Every line erases itself.

Minimal confirmation:

```c
waddstr(w, "LINE-A plain");     waddstr(w, "\n");
waddstr(w, "LINE-B with CR\r"); waddstr(w, "\n");
waddstr(w, "LINE-C plain");     waddstr(w, "\n");
```

renders `LINE-A plain`, a blank line, `LINE-C plain`.

Pre-existing since the TUI landed (#2) — it reproduces identically on that commit.

## Suggested approach

Strip a trailing `\r` as well as the `\n` in `helpme()`. Doing it in `tui_puts()` instead would be more defensive, since **any** output line ending in `\r` silently vanishes in full-screen mode — worth considering, and worth a note in AGENTS.md next to the existing "all output goes through `prout`" rule either way.

Note `sst.doc`'s CRLF endings are deliberate and preserved by convention; the fix belongs in the reader, not the file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `help move` (and other topics) shows the same documentation under `-t` as in plain mode.
- [ ] Paging through a long help topic works in both modes.
- [ ] Plain mode output is unchanged.
- [ ] `sst.doc` keeps its CRLF endings.
- [ ] Ideally a regression test, though this needs a pty — see #13.

## Notes

Found while reviewing the panel-staleness fix (#7). Testing needs tmux; see AGENTS.md.

Follow the workflow in [AGENTS.md](../blob/main/AGENTS.md).

ui-review turned a 12-line fix into a considerably better one. Three things it found beyond the original issue:

**The panels lied at the most dramatic moment in the game.** After a self-destruct they showed a healthy green Enterprise at full shields, energy 5000, right beside "your starship is now an expanding cloud of subatomic particles." **A display function was mutating game state.** `tui_refresh_panels()` called `newcnd()`, which writes the global `condit` — and `moving.c` deliberately sets `condit = IHRED` before a tractor beam takes hold, which a mid-turn repaint would hand straight back to GREEN. There's now a pure `condition_now()` that computes the answer without storing it, with `newcnd()` delegating to it so the rule has exactly one definition. That refactor made the rule unit-testable for the first time, and the existing test caught the change immediately: it had been asserting `condit = IHRED` renders as RED, which tested the plumbing rather than the rule. It now drives real game state, plus six new assertions including one that reading the condition doesn't write it.

**A frozen game showed blank panels** while its report printed, because the flag wasn't set until `setup()` returned. Flag ownership moved into `setup()` itself, which also covers that path.

Separately, I filed **#20** for a severe pre-existing bug it discovered: `help <command>` shows *nothing but blank lines* in full-screen mode — 1 non-blank line versus 21 in plain mode. `sst.doc` has CRLF endings, `helpme()` strips only the `\n`, and under ncurses the leftover `\r` makes each line erase itself. Fixes #7.

## What was wrong

The panels are meant to show the game as it stands. Three times they didn't:

- **Paged output** — stepping through a `[HIT SPACE BAR TO CONTINUE]` prompt left the panels older than the text beside them.
- **Replay** — starting a second game showed the *finished* game's quadrant and status through every setup question.
- **Destruction** — after the Enterprise was destroyed the panels went on reporting a healthy ship at full shields, next to the line about an expanding cloud of subatomic particles.

The last one was found in review; it's the same bug at the other end of the game, and it lands at the most dramatic beat in a playthrough.

## Why

The first two came from asking the wrong question. "Is there a game?" was answered with `d.date > 0.0` — but `setup()` doesn't overwrite the date until *after* it has asked the player everything, so a replay spent its entire setup showing the last game's numbers. The game knows when a game exists; it now says so explicitly, and `setup()` and `finish()` own that between them.

Blanking at the end needed a repaint as well as a flag. The panels keep their last painted content until something redraws them, and the epilogue prints before anything asks the player for input — so the flag alone left the dead ship on screen.

## A display that wrote to the game

Refreshing the panels used to call `newcnd()`, which recomputes the condition *and stores it*. A display has no business doing that, and it had a real consequence: `moving.c` sets the condition to RED by hand just before a tractor beam takes hold, and a repaint in that moment handed it back to GREEN — the game deciding you're in trouble, and the screen disagreeing.

The rule now has a version that answers without writing, with the old one defined in terms of it, so there's still exactly one rule. What the player sees is unchanged, because a short-range scan recomputes too.

Working the condition out in the open made it testable for the first time — which promptly caught a test that had been checking the wiring (`condit = IHRED` renders as RED) rather than the rule. It now drives real game state, with six new assertions including one that reading the condition doesn't write it.

## Verification

Review proved `condition_now()` equivalent to the original by brute force over the full boundary space — 891 combinations across galaxy/newstuf/energy including 99/100/101, 9/10/11 and 999/1000 — with zero mismatches, confirming the reordered checks preserve RED-beats-YELLOW precedence.

The paging fix was isolated by building a variant with only that line removed and driving both with the same seed: panel stardate **2300.6 with the fix, 2300.0 stale without**. Plain and `-f` output verified byte-identical to `main` across 48 seeded runs, 28 chosen specifically to reach RED and YELLOW. Every new assertion was mutation-tested.

A plain `quit` still leaves the panels up: the ship exists, the player simply stopped, and the next game blanks them anyway.

## Found on the way

**#20** — `help <command>` shows nothing but blank lines in full-screen mode; `sst.doc` is CRLF, and the leftover `\r` makes each line erase itself under ncurses. The whole manual is invisible to `-t` players. Pre-existing, filed separately.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
